perspective:
From Angela’s available perspective:

- I am Angela Hwang, a hairdresser with a doctorate; I know myself as ISFP.
- Kevin Flores is my close friend since high school. I know he works as a construction worker, and we often confide in each other about personal and professional matters.
- I noticed Kevin seemed unhappy with his job, so I invited him to coffee. He told me he was “alright,” just the usual grind, then admitted he was not happy, felt stuck and unfulfilled, and was going through the motions. I asked if he had considered a different job or career. He said he had, but felt overwhelmed and did not know where to start. I offered to look into options together; he accepted and thanked me.
- I believed he was considering a career change and felt supportive and hopeful. I found job openings and a career counseling service, shared them with him, and asked if he had thought more. He told me he was interested in something more creative, maybe design or architecture. I encouraged him to check the resources; he said he would and thanked me.
- I believed he was hesitant and felt frustrated and worried. I arranged a meeting with a career coach and told him. He said he appreciated it but was not sure he was ready. I encouraged him, and he agreed to give it a shot.
- I believed he was making progress and felt proud and relieved. I checked in. He told me the coach was helpful, he had started online courses in design, and he felt more confident. I offered more help; he said my support was enough and meant a lot to him.
- I believed he had successfully transitioned and felt happy and satisfied. I organized a small celebration party for his new career. He thanked me and said he was grateful and could not have done it without me. I told him he did the hard work and invited him to enjoy the party; he agreed.

I have no access to Kevin’s private thoughts or actions, or any events, beyond what he directly told me and what I observed or participated in.
